I’m thinking like this for my own land this year. I only have 12 mu, so I can’t spread money everywhere. I still keep wheat-maize on part of the land because grain is steady and it feeds the family first. But vegetables and stevia bring cash, so I keep some land in those too. I don’t study formulas. I look at what happened before, what the neighbors are doing, and whether I can still keep some cash in hand after buying seed, fertilizer, and water. Last year the well water cost more, so I won’t irrigate too freely. For wheat, if the stand looks good, I won’t push too much fertilizer. For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest, fast, no delay. For cabbage and cauliflower, if the market is not too bad, they still give quick money, but they need more care. Chili and eggplant take more labor, but if managed well they sell better than grain. Stevia is not for every farmer, but a few people nearby have kept it because the buyer still comes, so I will keep some area, not too much. I do things in a steady way, not too risky, and I use round numbers I know I can manage.

One thing to note: wheat and maize use the same 4 mu in double cropping, so the crop areas listed below add up to more than 12 mu over the whole year.
